claims.statement: PV operation and maintenance includes monitoring, analysis, maintenance services, reliability, and safety work, so a fault-resolution visit is a discrete operational event; the frequency and price for small Polish installers remain unverified.
The intended payer is the installer service function that already bears callback labor, travel, and customer-remedy costs; reservation-budget availability has not been demonstrated.
A founder entity can obtain bounded control by signing several six-month capacity reservations; UDT's public register supplies a lawful prospecting source but no right to any technician's time.
Poland's large reported prosumer microinstallation base supports the existence of an aftercare surface but does not establish an addressable overflow market.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Service manager or owner responsible for warranty and field operations
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Neutral multi-brand coverage and guaranteed local windows must outperform manufacturer-specific networks without requiring exclusivity
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Founder company owns the installer contract; each installer retains the end-customer relationship
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Installer referrals, public installer registries, wholesalers, and direct outreach after one separately contracted pilot

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Direct regional sales and reciprocal technician referrals; target recovery within two reservation months, unvalidated
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Reservation billed in advance; dispatches settled monthly after installer acceptance
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Target 20-35% on dispatches plus higher-margin reservation revenue; utilization and travel can materially erode it
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Central triage and quality review; phone coverage must be delegated rather than founder-on-call
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Contracting, liability insurance, qualification checks, health and safety procedures, and tax/accounting
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Hypothesis: 900-2500 PLN monthly reservation per installer plus 250-600 PLN routing margin per completed visit
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Technician payments, travel, consumables pass-through, scheduling software, and failed-visit credits

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Manufacturers, wholesalers, or large installers could expand authorized service networks or bundle overflow coverage
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Each overflow incident is a dispatchable paid service event; delay can also be measured as days to resolution, repeat visits, refunds, or retained installer labor
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Seasonal backlog, technician absence, geographic expansion, or repeated SLA misses
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Monthly reservation renewal and each completed dispatch

contrary_evidence: Installers may view third-party field work as a threat to quality, warranty status, or their customer relationship.
Public certification does not prove current competence, availability, insurance, or willingness to subcontract.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Nonexclusive six-month capacity-reservation agreements specifying hours, postcodes, response windows, rates, and for-cause termination
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Reserve smaller blocks from multiple unrelated technicians and narrow the initial service radius
critical_control_point.current_owner: Independent technicians and service firms control their calendars and qualifications
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Founder company owns the installer contract; each installer retains the end-customer relationship
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The parents' installer can be asked about lawful aftercare workflow and may independently buy a pilot, but it supplies no automatic customer, job, technician, contract, or confidential-data rights.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Founder company after counterparties sign scoped capacity-reservation contracts
critical_control_point.renewal: Rolling three-month renewal by mutual agreement
critical_control_point.subject: Monthly blocks of renewable-system diagnostic and repair capacity in named postcodes

economics.acquisition_route: One opt-in family-firm discovery pilot, then direct installer sales, technician referrals, and wholesalers
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, not forecast: 600 installer subscriptions at 1600 PLN monthly plus dispatch margin could exceed 12m PLN annual revenue; regional replication and delegated operations would be required for a plausible 5m PLN founder equity outcome
economics.founder_time: Founder designs routing and sells accounts within five hours daily; a paid dispatcher must cover operating windows before scale
economics.gross_margin_basis: Spread between contracted technician cost and dispatch price plus unused but prudently sized reservation revenue
economics.payback: Target under two months of reservation gross profit; unvalidated
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 900-2500 PLN monthly reservation plus a 250-600 PLN margin per completed dispatch
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual relationship if response time, resolution rate, and cost beat ad hoc subcontracting

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Dispatch-density, failure-code, route, and resolution-time data improve capacity placement and first-visit completion
fingerprint.customer: Small and midsize photovoltaic, battery, and heat-pump installers in western and central Poland
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Validate incident types through a voluntary family-installer relationship, then recruit unrelated installers and certified technicians from public registries and trade channels
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Geofenced overflow service using pre-reserved independent technician slots, standardized triage, and fixed dispatch pricing
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer pays a monthly capacity reservation and a fee when a technician is dispatched
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A cluster of faults, inspections, or warranty callbacks exceeds the installer's available field-service capacity

founder_fit: Routing, demand forecasting, and fault-code analysis use quantitative skills
The family operating relationship permits lawful workflow discovery without implying ownership
A dispatcher and standardized triage can cap founder involvement below five hours daily
Reservation utilization and response time are directly measurable
risks: Low utilization turns reserved hours into cash losses
A poor repair creates safety and warranty liability
Peak faults may correlate regionally, exhausting all reserved capacity
The model can become a labor-heavy dispatcher incompatible with part-time operation

structure.commercial_archetype: Contracted field-capacity operator earning reservation and dispatch fees
structure.control_point: Pre-reserved technician hours within defined service zones and response windows
structure.critical_dependency: A dependable replaceable pool of qualified independent technicians

thesis: Contract replaceable blocks of certified technician capacity before selling a monthly overflow guarantee and per-dispatch service to small renewable installers that cannot economically staff for peak fault demand.
title: Regional Renewable Aftercare Capacity Reserve
uncertainties: Incident density sufficient to keep reserved capacity economic
Acceptable response radius and travel reimbursement
Manufacturer authorization requirements by device category
Installer appetite for a fixed reservation fee
